applies_why: The judge text decides the Acts 2:30 dispute by treating the verse's failure to name the body's channel as leaving the point open rather than weighing the parties' chains by footing.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': one reading requires weighing the rival chains as wholes by their exhibited footing; the other permits finding the point open because the single verse Acts 2:30 does not itself name the channel.
why: The judge leaves the point open because Acts 2:30 alone does not name whose body is the channel, which is the retired verse-by-verse/stating-verse approach rather than a chain-against-chain footing comparison.
